tool.name: Salmon quantmerge
tool.description: Merge several quantification files into a single file
tool.command: #import re #set $counter = 0 #set $names = [] #for $input_data in $quantfiles: #set $counter += 1 mkdir ${counter}.quantmerge && ln -s '$input_data.quants' ${counter}.quantmerge/quant.sf && #if $input_data.names: #set $cleaned_name = re.sub('[^\w\-\s]', '_', str($input_data.names)) #set $_ = $names.append(str($cleaned_name)) #else: #set $cleaned_name = re.sub('[^\w\-\s]', '_', str($input_data.quants.element_identifier)) #set $_ = $names.append(str($cleaned_name)) #end if #end for salmon --no-version-check quantmerge --quants *.quantmerge --names #echo ' '.join($names)# --column '${column}' ${genes} #if str($missing): --missing '${missing}' #end if -o 'qmergeout.tab'

param.name: quants
param.label: Quantification file
param.help: This must be a quant.sf file, or a quant.genes.sf file if the genes option is enabled

param.name: names
param.label: Name for the sample in the merged output
param.help: If left empty the dataset name is used

param.label: Column to include in the output
param.help: The column that will be used to merge the files

param.label: Use gene-level quantification
param.help: If enabled, the input files will be treated as quant.genes.sf files instead of quant.sf

param.label: Missing Data Value
param.help: The value that will be used if a requested column is missing from one of the input files, e.g. 'NA'

tool.help:
@salmonhelp@
**Salmon quantmerge**
This tool merges the quantification results (e.g. the TPM or NumReads column) of several `quant.sf` files into a single tab-separated matrix, with one row per transcript and one column per sample.
The sample names can be set explicitly; otherwise the dataset names of the input files are used. A value to use for missing entries can be supplied (defaults to `NA` upstream).
Salmon 2.x is stricter than earlier versions about the input files: a `quant.sf` file that has a truncated row, uses a non-tab separator or repeats a target name is rejected instead of being filled with the missing-data value.
